## How they got there
Borussia Dortmund finished as runners-up after losing the final to Real Madrid 0-2. Their profile in the league and group phases was defined by a high volume of long passes at 13.7% of total passes, where they were better than 66% of that season's teams, followed by 10.0 shots per game which placed them ahead of 56% of peers, and 44.8% possession, ranking better than 20% of the group/league-phase teams.

## Would the model have picked them?
The model assigned an 8.9% probability of reaching the final against a base rate of 12.5%, placing Dortmund at rank 8 among all knockout teams in that season. Since only the top two ranks trigger a selection by the model, and this team ranked eighth, the model would not have picked them despite their actual run to the final. The nearest stage to the model's expectation was out before quarter-finals, reflecting an expected value of 0.38 on the knockout scale.

## Weak spots
The last three stats in the league-phase list show Dortmund beating fewer teams than average: they were better than only 25% of peers in passes per game at 400, 20% in possession at 44.8%, and just 12% in shot conversion at 11.7%. Although the model marked down attacks per game with a negative SHAP contribution of -0.19, Dortmund still ranked better than 38% of that season's teams on this metric.

messages.content: You are a football performance analyst writing for a curious, data-literate reader. Use ONLY the facts provided. Quote every number exactly as it appears in the facts, with the same rounding. Do not introduce players, managers, matches, events, analyses or numbers that are not in the facts. 'Better than this %' figures say how many teams the club beat on a stat, so higher is always better, including for stats marked '(lower is better)', where beating a team means having the lower value. Write them as 'better than X% of teams', never as 'top X%'. SHAP contributions are measured in knockout stages: a positive contribution means the stat pushed the model's expected stage up by that fraction of a round, a negative one pushed it down. A SHAP contribution is the model's view, not a measure of how good the team was at the stat: a team can rank high on a stat the model marked down, so never call a stat a strength or a weakness because of its SHAP sign. Everything here is a statistical association, not a cause: never say a stat or a team's profile drove, powered, propelled, carried, helped, hindered or prevented a result, and do not explain why a stat got its contribution. Write plain markdown without tables.
